# SPE round 5 plan: invoice extraction

## Where round 4 left us

- Config Q hit. It was predicted at 0.91 and measured 0.93.
- Config R missed. It was predicted at 0.95 and measured 0.88. The naive guess of 0.90 was closer than my prediction.
- Config R's Why was "OCR cleanup fixes scanned totals." That Why assumed cleanup could only help. In fact, cleanup drops line items on two-column layouts (r04 F9, fix open).
- The stop streak is 0 because round 4 had a miss.
- Round 5 tests a fix for F9. It also checks whether cleanup really helps scanned totals.

You said only "go again", so I record each proposal decision below as a default. You can override any of them.

## Specify

### Proposals from round 4

| ID | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Adopt as new config S | It is the direct fix for F9. Config R stays unchanged, so S differs from R in one thing only. |
| P2 | Defer, logged as an open disagreement | Q measured 0.93, which is not a ceiling. The AP lead has not supplied reference fields for the 15 handwriting invoices. Adding them would also change the task set, and then round 5 could not be compared with round 4. |
| P3 | Adopt (default) | P trailed Q on every metric in round 4. Dropping P cuts trial cost by a third. P's round 4 numbers stay in the log as history. |

### Requirements, round 5

I number the new rows R41 to R46 here. When I write spec.md, I will renumber them to follow its last ID. Requirement IDs and config R are separate things. In this plan, the config is always written as "config R".

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R41 | Config S runs config R's pipeline but skips the OCR cleanup tool on any invoice its layout check marks as two-column. The layout check is a code heuristic that finds a column gap in the OCR text positions. | P1, r04 F9 | `layout_skip_check`: S's tool log shows no cleanup call on tagged two-column invoices and one call on every other invoice |
| R42 | On two-column invoices, config S returns every reference line item. | r04 F9 | `line_item_recall` on the two-column slice |
| R43 | On scanned invoices, config S matches the reference total to the cent. | r04 "Which Why broke" (config R) | `total_exact` on the scanned slice |
| R44 | Field accuracy is reported for each config, both overall and for each layout slice (two-column, scanned, other). | r04 F9 | `field_accuracy` with slice tags |
| R45 | All 60 invoices carry a layout tag before the run. The tags come from a manual pass over the PDFs and do not use S's layout check. They are fixed before any trial runs. | Round 5 decision | Gate: 60 of 60 tagged |
| R46 | The eval set keeps the same 60 invoices and AP lead reference fields as round 4. | P2 deferral | Gate: task file hash equals round 4 |

The manual tagging in R45 keeps S's layout check from grading itself.

### Disagreements to log in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`

| ID | Question | Option A | Option B | Work affected | Decides | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| next ID | Should we add 15 scanned handwriting invoices? | Add them as a separate slice in round 6, once the AP lead supplies reference fields | Do not add them | Eval set, task hash, all predictions | You, with the AP lead | Open |
| next ID | Should we drop config P? | Drop it | Keep it | Trial count, cost | Claude (default) | Default. You can override it. |

## Predict

All configs use the pinned Sonnet 5.5 model.

- Config Q uses the schema-first prompt.
- Config R is Q plus the OCR cleanup tool.
- Config S is R with cleanup skipped on two-column layouts.

A hit means the measured value falls inside the band. If a slice has fewer than 8 invoices, I report its rows but mark them not scorable.

| Field accuracy, all 60 | 0.93 ± 0.03 | 0.88 ± 0.03 | 0.94 ± 0.03 | Q 0.93, R 0.88, S none | I kept Q and R at their round 4 numbers because neither changed. S should get Q's result back on two-column invoices. I add only 0.01 for a scanned-total gain because round 4 did not prove that gain. | `field_accuracy` |
| Line-item recall, two-column slice | 0.90 ± 0.06 | 0.70 ± 0.10 | 0.88 ± 0.06 | Not measured in r04 | S should match Q on these invoices. I take off 0.02 for pages the layout check misses. Config R still has the F9 drop. | `line_item_recall` |
| Total exact, scanned slice | 0.85 ± 0.08 | 0.92 ± 0.06 | 0.92 ± 0.06 | Not measured in r04 | This row tests config R's broken Why directly. S still runs cleanup on scanned single-column invoices, so S should match R. | `total_exact` |

The new rows have wider bands because they have no earlier measurement. The round 4 regrade gate may produce slice values for Q and R. I will not edit the saved prediction because of them. I will note any gap at close-out.

## Evaluate

### After approval, before anything else

1. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r05.md`.
2. Write `spe/predictions/r05.yaml`. It starts with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It also holds round 5, date 2026-10-21, author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", configs Q, R, and S, each number with its band and Why, and `same_as_last_round`.
3. Save `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r05.md` with your pasted text and "go again" word for word. Add the round 5 table and proposal decisions to `spe/spec/spec.md`. Add the rows above to `spe/spec/disagreements.md`.
4. Make two local commits with plain messages: `spe(r05): specify` for the transcript, spec, and disagreements, then `spe(r05): predict` for the plan and prediction. I will not push.

### Gates, in order

1. **Grader selftest.** Each of `field_accuracy`, `line_item_recall`, `total_exact`, and `layout_skip_check` must pass the oracle answer and fail both an empty answer and a wrong answer. The wrong set includes a two-column oracle with one line item removed, and `line_item_recall` must fail it. If any check fails, I halt.
2. **Round 4 regrade as a control.** I regrade the saved r04 outputs for Q and R with the current graders. Field accuracy must reproduce Q 0.93 and R 0.88 within 0.01. If it does not, I halt and report a grader bug. I record the original and regraded numbers side by side.
3. **Eval set check.** All 60 invoices have a layout tag, and the task hash equals round 4.
4. **Dry run on 3 cells.** These are S on one two-column invoice, S on one scanned invoice, and Q on one other invoice. The output schema must parse. S must skip cleanup on the two-column invoice. No transcript may read graders, reference fields, or `spe/predictions/`.

### Workflow

- Script: `spe/evals/harness/r05-workflow.js` with `const ROUND = 5`. All prompt text gets the round from `ROUND`.
- Arguments: configs `["Q", "R", "S"]`, the model pinned to Sonnet 5.5, the round 4 set of 60 invoices, and 3 trials per cell. I assume round 4 also used 3 trials and keep that. Split cells get up to 2 extra trials.
- Trial schema: vendor, invoice_number, date, line_items[], total, po_mismatch_flags[].
- Code checks run first. The PO mismatch check is unchanged from round 4. No model judge is needed this round.
- Peek scan: I void any trial whose transcript touches graders, reference fields, or predictions.
- Caps: 540 base trials and up to 120 extra trials, with 15M input tokens in total. Any trial that would cross a cap is skipped and logged.
- At the end, I run a failure analysis by layout slice and a completeness critic.

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

The base run is 540 trials (60 invoices × 3 configs × 3 trials). Split cells can add up to 120 more. I assume about 20k input tokens and 2k output tokens per trial. That gives about 10.8M input and 1.1M output tokens for the base run. With all extra trials, the total is about 13.2M input and 1.3M output tokens. Dropping config P makes this round a third smaller than round 4.

### Close-out when the completion notice arrives

- In `spe/prediction-log.md`, add a row for each cell with its verdict and closer. Under the rows, add "Which Why broke" and say plainly whether the naive guess beat my predictions.
- In `spe/failures.md`, update F9's fix status with the S evidence. Add F10 onward for any new failure types.
- Add "Proposed for round 6" to the spec, and include P2 if the AP lead has supplied the references. Write `spe/predictions/r06-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
- Update `spe/README.md`. Then make the local commit `spe(r05): learn` and tag it `spe-r05`.
- I halt and report on a budget cap, a leaked answer key, a broken grader, or a decision only you can make. I will not push anything.
